title: Module 9 · Stroke
intro: Stroke alert checks, tenecteplase and alteplase dosing and safety, contraindications and imaging selected windows, angioedema, post lytic care, DAPT, ICH reversal and BP, and nimodipine after SAH.

cases.title: Stroke alert: the pharmacist checks
cases.stem: Stroke alert. Last known well 2 hours ago. Weight 82 kg (measured). BP 196/108. Glucose 132. On no anticoagulants.

steps.q: Can the thrombolytic be given now?

options.t: Not yet: BP must be below 185/110 first
options.why: Treat the BP, then give the lytic.

options.t: Labetalol 10 to 20 mg IV over 1 to 2 minutes (may repeat once)
Nicardipine infusion 5 mg/h, titrate by 2.5 mg/h every 5 to 15 minutes (max 15 mg/h)
Low glucose (below 50) can mimic a stroke

cases.pearl: **Before lytics: BP below 185/110, glucose checked, weight, last anticoagulant dose.**

sources.t: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (Top Things to Know)
St. Mary's stroke alert protocol, thrombolytic dosing chart and reversal order set (verify locally)

cases.title: Tenecteplase dose
cases.stem: BP is now 176/98. The team chooses tenecteplase. Weight 82 kg.

options.t: 0.25 mg/kg IV bolus over 5 seconds, max 25 mg: 20.5 mg
options.why: Many sites use a weight band chart; follow it.
The STEMI dose is double. A classic, dangerous mix up.

steps.q: Tenecteplase or alteplase per the 2026 guideline?

options.t: Either is endorsed in the 4.5 hour window
options.why: Tenecteplase is a single bolus, which reduces mixing and infusion errors.

steps.q: What safety steps do you take when preparing it?

options.t: Independent double check of drug (tenecteplase vs alteplase) and dose, and waste the excess so only the stroke dose is in the syringe
options.why: Look alike packaging and the 50 mg vial are known risks.
Tenecteplase can precipitate with dextrose; use normal saline.

cases.pearl: **TNK stroke: 0.25 mg/kg, max 25 mg, over 5 seconds. Never the cardiac dose.**

sources.t: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (Top Things to Know)

cases.title: Alteplase math

steps.q: What are the total, bolus and infusion amounts?

options.t: Total 63 mg (0.9 mg/kg); bolus 6.3 mg over 1 minute; 56.7 mg over 60 minutes

options.why: 90 mg is the cap, not the dose.

steps.q: What happens to the extra drug in the vial?

options.t: Remove and waste the excess before hanging the bag so the patient cannot get more than the calculated dose
options.why: Overdose risk if the whole vial is infused.

cases.pearl: **Alteplase: 0.9 mg/kg (max 90), 10% bolus, 90% over 60 minutes. Waste the excess.**

sources.t: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (Top Things to Know)

cases.title: Who should NOT get a thrombolytic?

steps.q: Which patients should not get a thrombolytic?

options.t: Mild, nondisabling symptoms that do not affect daily activities
options.why: Not recommended for mild nondisabling stroke.

options.t: Last known well 2 hours ago, BP 170/90, no anticoagulant, disabling deficit

steps.q: A patient woke up with symptoms (unknown onset). Is thrombolysis ever possible?

options.t: Yes, in selected patients with advanced imaging (for example DWI FLAIR or perfusion mismatch), up to about 9 hours

cases.pearl: **No lytic: recent DOAC, INR above 1.7, platelets below 100k, mild nondisabling symptoms.**

sources.t: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (Top Things to Know)
Guideline Central: Feb 2026 AHA/ASA early management of acute ischemic stroke spotlight

cases.title: Tongue swelling during alteplase
cases.stem: The patient takes lisinopril. Tongue and lips are swelling.

options.t: Orolingual angioedema; plasmin raises bradykinin and ACE inhibitors block its breakdown
Stop the infusion; methylprednisolone, diphenhydramine and famotidine; epinephrine if worsening; icatibant or C1 esterase inhibitor may be considered; protect the airway

cases.pearl: **Lytic + ACE inhibitor + swelling: stop, steroid, H1, H2, epi if worse.**

sources.t: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (Top Things to Know)

cases.title: After the thrombolytic
cases.stem: Two hours after tenecteplase, an order for aspirin 325 mg and enoxaparin 40 mg appears.

options.t: No antithrombotics for 24 hours after thrombolysis (unless specifically indicated), usually until a repeat scan

steps.q: What BP goal applies for the first 24 hours?

options.why: Intensive lowering below 140 is not recommended (2026).

cases.pearl: **After lytic: BP below 180/105, no antithrombotics for 24 hours.**

sources.t: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (Top Things to Know)
Guideline Central: Feb 2026 AHA/ASA early management of acute ischemic stroke spotlight

cases.title: Minor stroke: DAPT
cases.stem: Minor ischemic stroke, NIHSS 3, no thrombolytic, no atrial fibrillation.

options.t: Aspirin plus clopidogrel for 21 days (clopidogrel 300 to 600 mg load, then 75 mg; aspirin load then 81 mg), then one antiplatelet
options.why: 2026 update allows NIHSS up to 5 and starts within 72 hours.

options.t: Aspirin plus clopidogrel for a year

cases.pearl: **Minor stroke: DAPT 21 days, high intensity statin.**

sources.t: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (Top Things to Know)

cases.title: ICH on apixaban
cases.stem: ICH. Apixaban last taken 5 hours ago. SBP 196. Weight 80 kg.

options.t: 4F-PCC (commonly 50 units/kg, 4,000 units, or a fixed dose per protocol)
Target SBP about 140 (range 130 to 150); avoid below 130

steps.q: Should she get platelets if she also takes aspirin?

options.t: No, unless going to neurosurgery (PATCH: harm with transfusion)

cases.pearl: **ICH: reverse fast, SBP to 140 (not below 130), no platelets for antiplatelet bleeds unless surgery.**

sources.t: Greenberg SM, et al. 2022 AHA/ASA guideline for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage. Stroke 2022;53:e282-e361
Baharoglu MI, et al. Platelet transfusion vs standard care after ICH on antiplatelet therapy (PATCH). Lancet 2016;387:2605-2613

cases.title: ICH on warfarin or heparin
cases.stem: Two patients with ICH: (A) warfarin, INR 3.1, 90 kg; (B) heparin infusion at 1,400 units/h for the last 3 hours.

options.t: 4F-PCC 25 units/kg (INR 2 to below 4): 2,250 units + vitamin K 10 mg IV
About 42 mg (1 mg per 100 units given in the last 2 to 3 hours: 4,200 units), max 50 mg
options.why: Give slowly; watch for hypotension and anaphylaxis.

cases.pearl: **Warfarin: PCC by INR + vit K. Heparin: protamine 1 mg per 100 units (last 2 to 3 h, max 50).**

sources.t: Greenberg SM, et al. 2022 AHA/ASA guideline for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage. Stroke 2022;53:e282-e361
Kcentra prescribing information, DailyMed

cases.title: Nimodipine after SAH
cases.stem: Aneurysmal SAH. The patient has an NG tube. A nurse asks to draw nimodipine liquid into a syringe.

options.t: Nimodipine 60 mg orally or by tube every 4 hours for 21 days; 30 mg every 2 hours if BP drops

steps.q: What is the critical safety step?

options.t: Use an oral or enteral syringe that cannot connect to IV lines, labeled for oral use only
options.why: IV injection of capsule contents has caused deaths (boxed warning).

options.t: A standard luer lock syringe is fine

cases.pearl: **Nimodipine 60 mg q4h x 21 days, enteral syringe only. Never IV.**
